gold: This analysis reveals that test repeatability is fundamentally about managing uncertainty in our knowledge systems. Non-repeatable tests introduce epistemic doubt - when a test fails, we cannot immediately know whether we've found a bug or encountered randomness. The mathematical formalization shows that even small amounts of non-determinism ($\rho \lt 0.9$) can double or triple debugging time, validating the intuition that flaky tests are among the most expensive technical debts.
